cases.statement: Two brothers of Turkish origin (patients #1 and #2), both homozygous. Table columns are patients #1 to #4 in order; patients #1 and #2 are the first and second values in each row.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level: both brothers have undetectable HDL and ApoA-I, splenomegaly and thrombocytopenia (attributed to hypersplenism); patient #1 had orange tonsils. The main text does not describe the genetic test used or exclusion of other genes; details are in supplemental materials not available here.

quotes.quote: | Orange tonsils | Yes, history of tonsillectomy | History of tonsillectomy due to chronic tonsillitis | No | Unclear, history of tonsillectomy |
In contrast to the clinical presentation, standard lipid parameters were similar including thrombocytopenia (due to hypersplenism)
A detailed presentation of all cases is presented in the supplemental materials (17).

segregation.statement: Two affected brothers are both homozygous. All tested relatives of patients #1 and #2 were heterozygous with reduced HDL; the main text does not give the number of relatives or which relatives (parents not named), and refers to supplementary Fig. S4 / Table 1 (not available here). An uncle had premature CVD (genotype not reported).

quotes.quote: Specifically, all first-degree relatives that were available and consented to further testing were genotyped for the described variants, and their lipid profiles were analyzed [Supplementary Fig. S4, Supplementary Table 1 (17)].
Of note, all relatives of patients #1 + 2 were heterozygous for the c.2418G > A loss-of-function variant with associated reduced HDL levels.

in_trans.statement: Homozygous in both brothers. First-degree relatives tested were heterozygous, but the main text does not say whether both parents were among them; consanguinity not reported.

quotes.quote: | Mutation (homozygous) | c.2418G > A | c.2418G > A | c.679C > T, p.(Arg227Ter) | c.5055del, p.(Lys1685AsnfsTer9) |
Of note, all relatives of patients #1 + 2 were heterozygous for the c.2418G > A loss-of-function variant with associated reduced HDL levels.

functional.statement: No assay of this variant is reported. The authors state that functional analyses were not available (said of the proposed lipid-metabolism mechanisms).

quotes.quote: Also, discussed mechanisms regulating lipid metabolisms must be regarded as hypotheses, as functional analyses were not available.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Per the batch HGVS, c.2418G>A is predicted to be a nonsense (stop-gain) variant, p.(Trp806Ter); the paper gives no protein change. The authors call it a loss-of-function variant and describe TD as caused by ABCA1 loss of function.

quotes.quote: Genetic testing confirmed homozygous loss-of-function variants in ABCA1 (c.2418G > A in patients #1 and #2, c.679C > T in patient #3, and c.5055del in patient #4, all regarded as American College of Medical Genetics class 5 (pathogenic).

Specifically, loss-of-function variants in ABCA1 lead to intracellular cholesterol accumulation in the reticuloendothelial system and peripheral macrophages (“foam cells”), which may infiltrate various organs and essentially contribute to the development of atherosclerosis (7).

population_data_in_papers.statement: No frequency data for this variant. The authors state it was previously undescribed (novelty statement, not population data).

quotes.quote: Two previously undescribed variants (c.2418G > A, c.5055.del) were reported.

authors_classification.statement: Authors classify it as ACMG class 5 (pathogenic) in both brothers; individual ACMG criteria are not listed.

notes_for_panel: Two homozygous brothers with biochemically typical TD; relatives reported heterozygous with reduced HDL (numbers in a supplement not available here). Authors' ACMG class 5. No functional, in-silico or population data in the main text.
